Name: Tyrannosaurus ‭(‬Tyrant lizard‭)Phonetic: Ty-ran-no-sore-usNamed By: Henry Fairfield Osborn‭ ‬-‭ ‬1905.Synonyms: Dinotyrannus megagracilis,‭ ‬Dynamosaurus imperiosus,‭ ‬Manospondylus gigas,‭ ‬Stygivenator molnari.Classification: Chordata,‭ ‬Reptilia,‭ ‬Dinosauria,‭ ‬Saurischia,‭ ‬Theropoda,‭ ‬Tyrannosauria,‭ ‬Tyrannosauridae.Species: T. rex (type)Type: Carnivore.Size: Most complete specimen 12.3 meters long, isolated remains suggest a potential upper size of around 13 meters long.Known locations: Western North America.Time period: Late Campanian/Early Maastrichtian of the Cretaceous.Fossil representation: Over‭ ‬30‭ ‬individuals are known,‭ ‬some forming almost complete skeletons.
Tyrannosaurus rex has been known to science since the end of the nineteenth century,‭ ‬and to this day remains arguably the most popular dinosaur the world over.‭ ‬This is evidenced by its almost mandatory inclusion in books,‭ ‬TV shows,‭ ‬games and websites that are about dinosaurs in general.‭ ‬Tyrannosaurus also probably has more toys and merchandising relating to it than any other dinosaur.

Name: Triceratops ‭(‬Three horned face‭)‬.Phonetic: Tri-seh-rah-tops.Named By: Othniel Charles Marsh‭ ‬-‭ ‬1889.Synonyms: Bison alticornis,‭ ‬Sterrholophus,‭ ‬Ugrosaurus.‭Possible additional synonyms:‭ Claorhynchus,‭ ‬Diceratus‭ (‬synonym of Nedoceratops‭)‬,‭ ‬Nedoceratops,‭ ‬Ojoceratops,‭ ‬Tatankaceratops,‭ ‬Torosaurus.Species synonyms: T.‭ ‬brevicornus,‭ ‬T.‭ ‬calicornis,‭ ‬T.‭ ‬elatus,‭ ‬T.‭ ‬flabellatus,‭ ‬T.‭ ‬mortuarius,‭ ‬T.‭ ‬obtusus,‭ ‬T.‭ ‬serratus,‭ ‬T.‭ ‬sylvestris.Classification: Chordata,‭ ‬Reptilia,‭ ‬Dinosauria,‭ ‬Ornithischia,‭ ‬Ceratopsia,‭ ‬Ceratopsidae,‭ ‬Chasmosaurinae,‭ ‬Triceratopsini.Species: T.‭ ‬horridus‭ (‬type‭)‬,‭ ‬T.‭ ‬prorsus.Dubious species: T.‭ ‬albertensis,‭ ‬T.‭ ‬alticornis,‭ ‬T.‭ ‬eurycephalus,‭ ‬T.‭ ‬galeus,‭ ‬T.‭ ‬hatcheri,‭ ‬T.‭ ‬ingens,‭ ‬T.‭ ‬maximus,‭ ‬T.‭ ‬sulcatus.Diet: Herbivore.Size: Estimated between‭ ‬8‭ ‬to‭ ‬9‭ ‬meters long.Known locations: USA,‭ ‬Colorado,‭ ‬Montana,‭ ‬South Dakota,‭ ‬Wyoming.‭ ‬Canada,‭ ‬Alberta,‭ ‬Saskatchewan.Time period: Late Maastrichtian of the Cretaceous.Fossil representation: Multiple remains,‭ ‬some of almost complete individuals.
When it comes to popularity Triceratops is only eclipsed by Tyrannosaurus,‭ ‬and even then there are a considerable portion of people who actually prefer Triceratops over the aforementioned apex predator.‭ ‬Yet despite its frequent depiction from toys to dinosaur books,‭ ‬films and other media,‭ ‬there is still a lot of controversy and misconception surrounding this much loved dinosaur.
How Triceratops looked in life       Triceratops is one of the few dinosaurs that hardly need a description.‭ ‬Like with other large ceratopsian dinosaurs it was a quadrupedal‭ (‬four legged‭) ‬herbivore that had a proportionately large skull in relation to its total body size,‭ ‬just under a third of the total length.‭ ‬The skull was adorned with a short neck frill that rose up from the back,‭ ‬and three horns.‭ ‬The largest horns were the two that rose up from above the eyes and reached up to one meter long,‭ ‬while the nasal horn that pointed up from the snout was much smaller.‭ ‬Some specimens of Triceratops sometimes have epoccipitals‭ (‬small pointed bones‭) ‬that are attached to the edge of the frill.‭ ‬Triceratops was once classed as a centrosaurine ceratopsian dinosaur because of this small frill,‭ ‬but today it is considered to be a‭ ‬chasmosaurine‭ (‬often alternatively referred to as ceratopsine‭) ‬on the basis of the well-developed brow horns that are usually greatly reduced or absent in centrosaurines.‭ ‬The frill itself is still interesting because its short and solid which makes it very different from other known genera that usually have long frills with holes in them.‭ ‬However this feature may yet have greater ramifications for Triceratops and some other ceratopsian dinosaur genera‭ (‬click to skip down to this‭)‬.       Like with other ceratopsian dinosaurs there has been some confusion as to how Triceratops stood and walked.‭ ‬Earlier reconstructions took into account the large skulls with the idea that the fore legs would have to sprawl out to the sides to support the bulk.‭ ‬Track ways suggested different however,‭ ‬that the fore legs were not sprawled which led to the question of‭ ‘‬did Triceratops have sprawling or upright legs‭?’‬.‭ ‬The simple answer is a little of both as modern reconstructions including computer modelling have revealed that the fore legs were upright but with the elbows bowed out to the sides.       Another interesting feature is the way the fore feet‭ (‬equivalent to your hands‭) ‬rested on the ground.‭ ‬Unlike thereophorans‭ (‬stegosaurs and ankylosaurs‭) ‬and sauropods‭ (‬quadrupedal long necked dinosaurs‭) ‬the fingers pointed out to the sides rather than facing forwards.‭ ‬Although a primitive trait this actually reveals that the direct ancestors of the large late Cretaceous ceratopsian dinosaurs were actually bipedal‭ (‬walked upon two legs‭) ‬with their hands more for grasping and support rather than weight bearing.       One of the most exciting discoveries associated with Triceratops is a skin impression which also reveals the presence of bristle like fibres.‭ ‬Although this may appear strange,‭ ‬especially to those who have grown up with images of Triceratops being a relatively smooth skinned creature,‭ ‬earlier ceratopsians are thought to have had bristle like extensions on areas like the tail.‭ ‬This has been confirmed by some fossils from China and is especially poignant considering that the popular consensus is that primitive ceratopsian dinosaurs first appeared here towards the end of the Jurassic period.‭ ‬If these bristle structures were indeed present upon Triceratops,‭ ‬then it‭’‬s also plausible that other ceratopsian dinosaur genera between it and the primitive forms may have also had them

A replica of the vial from Jurassic Park in which Dennis Nedry steals to put into the barbasol can. Sobek (also called Sebek) was an ancient Egyptian deity with a complex and fluid nature. He is associated with the Nile crocodile or the West African crocodile and is represented either in its form or as a human with a crocodile head. Sobek was also associated with pharaonic power, fertility, and military prowess, but served additionally as a protective deity with apotropaic qualities, invoked especially for protection against the dangers presented by the Nile. - source - Wikipedia

Godzilla black
Godzilla, the iconic kaiju, stands as a towering figure in cinematic history, captivating audiences worldwide with its colossal presence and enduring legacy. The name Godzilla originates from the Japanese word Gojira, meaning strange beast, a fitting moniker for this enigmatic creature. First introduced to audiences in the 1954 film Godzilla, this behemoth emerged from the depths of the Pacific Ocean, a consequence of mankind's experimentation with nuclear power during the post-war era.Throughout the decades, Godzilla has evolved beyond its original depiction as a symbol of nuclear devastation, transcending its origins to embody various themes and narratives. While initially portrayed as a relentless force of destruction, decimating cities with its sheer power and ferocity, Godzilla's character has undergone nuanced interpretations, sometimes portrayed as a reluctant hero or a guardian of Earth, defending humanity from other monstrous threats.The creature's physical appearance is unmistakable, characterized by its towering stature, reptilian features, and dorsal plates that emit an eerie glow before unleashing devastating atomic breath. Its immense size and strength make it a formidable opponent, capable of withstanding military attacks and rivaling other legendary creatures in epic battles that shake the very foundations of the earth.Yet, amidst the chaos and destruction it often leaves in its wake, Godzilla has also inspired awe and admiration, symbolizing resilience in the face of adversity and the power of nature unleashed. Its complex portrayal reflects humanity's own relationship with nature, technology, and the consequences of our actions.Whether portrayed as a force of nature wreaking havoc or a noble protector standing against existential threats, Godzilla continues to captivate audiences, its legacy enduring through countless films, television series, comics, and cultural references. As one of cinema's most enduring icons, Godzilla remains a testament to the enduring power of imagination and the timeless appeal of larger-than-life storytelling.

Introducing the Prehistoric Howler Launcher, a unique and imaginative 3D asset that blurs the lines between weaponry and ancient relics. description_text:
Long before the first dinosaurs ever roamed the Earth, the apex predator of the Permian period ruled the ancient swamps and forests — the Dimetrodon. With its large sail and powerful jaws, this early synapsid was a formidable presence in its ecosystem. In this model, the Dimetrodon is captured in a dynamic pose, with lifelike skin textures and an imposing sail that reflects its iconic appearance.
This 3D model is a faithful interpretation, ideal for collectors of prehistoric creatures, educational dioramas, or tabletop gaming with a paleontological twist. The design ensures all parts of the creature, including its detailed teeth and sail fin, are clearly visible and well defined.
Please note that the model is primarily designed for textured versions (OBJ + MTL in ZIP archive), allowing for a rich and visually detailed result when used with color-supported 3D printing or digital rendering. The non-textured version (STL, 3MF) may lack some surface details visible in the textured formats.

Recommended Material: PLA, PETG, or resin (for better surface definition)

Supports Required: Yes (especially for the sail and teeth)
Recommended Layer Height: 0.12–0.2mm
Infill: 10–15%
Formats Included: STL, OBJ, MTL, 3MF, FBX, BLEND (all in ZIP archive)
3D Viewer Files: STL and OBJ included separately for instant preview compatibility
Scaling Note:This model is designed in millimeters (mm). If it appears too small when imported into your slicer, ensure your software is set to mm units. If needed, scale the model up 100x if the slicer defaults to meters instead.

Nerathor is an ancient nightmare creature born from a realm of darkness. It feeds on fear and thrives in abandoned, lightless places. Its form appears like semi-solid smoke, shifting slightly as it moves, giving it an eerie, ethereal presence.

Its legs are reptilian, like those of a raptor, allowing it to move with speed and agility. A long, serpent-like tail trails behind, ending in a natural axe-shaped bone blade—its primary weapon.
Bone-like blades protrude from its back like skeletal wings. As it moves, dark mist trails behind, and the faint sound of whispering voices follows its path. Its eyes, runes, and glowing heart light up in the dark, giving it an ominous presence in any environment.

description_text:
High above the emerald canopies of Aevaris, the Draconian Skyguard soars as the vigilant protector of the Verdant Pact’s skies. Born of scaled heritage and sworn to the Pact’s ancient oaths, these winged sentinels patrol the borders where wind and forest meet, their keen eyes ever watchful for threats from beyond.
Clad in layered armor shaped from living metal and the bones of sky-serpents, each Skyguard wields the Stormlance—a weapon forged to harness the fury of tempests. With every beat of their great wings, they stir the air in warning to trespassers, while to allies, their presence brings reassurance and steadfast loyalty.
Legends say the Skyguard answer not only to the Verdant Pact’s council but also to the whisper of the wind itself, hearing its call to rise in defense long before mortal eyes could see danger. Whether in the clash of battle or in the quiet vigil of twilight, they are the embodiment of the Pact’s promise: the sky shall never fall unguarded.
This model is based on an original concept and design. The initial 3D form was generated with the assistance of AI tools, after which it was extensively refined and manually detailed in Blender and other 3D editing software. This workflow ensures the figure maintains its unique character and meets the standards of precision, structure, and print-readiness required for high-quality 3D printing.
Please note that the model is primarily designed for textured versions (OBJ + MTL in ZIP archive), allowing for a rich and visually detailed result when used with color-supported 3D printing or digital rendering. The non-textured version (STL, 3MF) may lack some surface details visible in the textured formats.
Technical Features & Printing Recommendations:
Recommended Print Settings: 0.1–0.15 mm layer height for best detail; infill 15–20%
Supports Required: Yes, especially for wings and overhanging armor parts
Recommended Size: 100–150 mm height for standard tabletop scale; can be scaled up for display
Recommended Materials: PLA, ABS, or resin for fine detail
Minimum Print Time: ~420 minutes at 100 mm height
Material Usage: ~65–90 g at 100 mm height
Scaling Note: This model is designed in millimeters (mm). If it appears too small when imported into your slicer, ensure your software is set to mm units. If needed, scale the model up 100x if the slicer defaults to meters instead.

description_text:
The mugger crocodile (Crocodylus palustris), also called marsh crocodile, broad-snouted crocodile and mugger, is a crocodilian native to freshwater habitats from southern Iran to the Indian subcontinent. It is extinct in Bhutan and Myanmar and has been listed as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List since 1982.[2]
It is a medium-sized crocodile that inhabits lakes, rivers, marshes and artificial ponds. Both young and adult mugger crocodiles dig burrows where they retreat when temperature drops below 5 °C (41 °F) or exceeds 38 °C (100 °F). Females dig holes in the sand as nesting sites and lay up to 46 eggs during the dry season.[3][4][5] of hatchlings depends on temperature during incubation.[6] It preys on fish, reptiles, birds and mammals. Young feed on insects.[7][8]
It is one of three crocodilians in India, apart from saltwater crocodile (C. porosus) and gharial (Gavialis gangeticus).[9]

description_text:
MÉDARD STRETCHED By Modular Lighting InstrumentsCollectionMédardTypeLED adjustable ceiling spotlightMaterialsPowder Coated AluminiumDesignersBasten LeijhManufacture year2019Our popular Médard is taking its design to new lengths.‎ Already appreciated for its high versatility - thanks to its orientable head - Médard Stretched will be even more valued, with its new tubes available in two sizes.‎ Spaces with very large and high ceilings, such as hospitality environments, will be perfect to host Médard Stretched’s elegant form.‎
TWO NEW SIZES, RELIABLE COMPATIBILITYMédard Stretched comes in two new adjustable tube lengths.‎ The first is 300mm, and the second, 500mm, even holds two light units; the same Médard units we already know and love.‎ Also available in white and black structure, Médard’s lamp units can still flaunt their flexibility of h355º and v365º.‎
GEAR INTEGRATED OR EXCLUDEDThe light units come in two versions.‎ One is with trailing edge dimming, with the gear integrated (GI) and a connection box on the ceiling.‎ The gear excluded (GE) version has a more minimalistic approach.‎ This design shows a thin ceiling plate and offers a selection of dimming protocols.‎
CONSISTENT COLOURS, AMBIENT LED DIMMINGAvailable in the same tranquil white and black structures, Médard Stretched will match the existing Médards that already beautify large spaces.‎ Lumen output per lamp unit is 936lm, and power consumption is 13W.‎ Units include a trailing edge dimming system.‎
Nature is always the best inspiration for great designs.‎ The insect stick inspired the Dutch design agency Bleijh in the design and creation of Médard.‎ The quircky nature fits the Modular DNA.‎ Médard is highly versatile thanks to its orientable head.‎ The track mounted and ceiling mounted versions are the perfect example of the architectural lighting portfolio of Modular.‎ Médard is LED dedicated and powerful enough to accentuate objects in the room.‎ Also great company to have next to your bed or on your desk.‎
Now also available with warm dim.

description_text:
Butterfly egg from the species known as Holly blue or chalkhill blue, (Polyommatus coridon), high quality model. With just the right amount of polygons to make it look soft. Subdivided, made from solid parts, it can 3D printed, stl file included. It will accept perfectly different types of materials, all metal, cheap plastic, or crystal. 

  - Watertight parts.

  - Quads and tris mix.

  - Remove the middle bar and keep one clip to make a small accessory hanger such as socks and scarfs.

The model is not to scale. Real size can be of under half a millimeter or 0.03 "

  - The model is originally made in Modo, other software may require material edits.

  - Formats included: .lwo, .obj, .fbx, .stl, .lxo (.obj contains UV information and is an industry standard that most software can use)

Included are textures. There is a color map and a normal map.

  - Includes a .stl file for physical recreation, like 3d printing.

  - Includes a high subdivision version and different formats are available upon request.

KAWS is a multi-faceted artist straddling the worlds of art and design in his prolific body of work that ranges from paintings, murals, and large-scale sculptures to product design and toy-making. His iconic “XX” signature has its roots in the beginning of his career as a street artist in the 1990s, when he began altering found advertisements by incorporating his own masterful paintings. Evoking the sensibilities of Pop artists like Andy Warhol and Claes Oldenburg, KAWS possesses a sophisticated humor and thoughtful interplay with consumer products and collaborations with global brands. description_text:
A realistic 3D grass model is a digital representation of natural grass created for use in 3D computer graphics and visualization applications. This type of model is designed to mimic the appearance and behavior of real grass in a three-dimensional virtual environment, such as video games, architectural renderings, or animated films. Here's a detailed description of what a realistic 3D grass model typically entails:
Detailed Geometry: The 3D grass model starts with intricate geometry that replicates the individual blades of grass. Each blade is typically created as a slender, elongated polygon or mesh. The geometry often includes variations in height, thickness, and curvature to achieve a natural look.
Texturing: Realistic 3D grass models feature high-quality textures that emulate the appearance of grass blades. These textures include intricate details such as tiny leaf veins, color variations, and even imperfections like insect damage or dirt smudges to enhance realism.
Material Properties: The grass material used in the 3D model is essential for achieving realism. It includes properties like diffuse color, specular reflection, and transparency to accurately simulate how grass interacts with light.
Wind Animation: To mimic the swaying motion of grass in the wind, realistic 3D grass models often incorporate animation. These models may have dynamic animations or wind maps that determine how each blade of grass moves with environmental conditions.
Density and Variation: Natural grass doesn't grow uniformly, so a realistic 3D grass model usually incorporates variations in blade density, height, and color to emulate the randomness found in real-world grassy areas.
Interaction with Other Objects: Realistic grass should interact with other 3D objects in the scene. This includes casting realistic shadows, bending or flattening when characters or objects move through it, and responding to changes in lighting conditions.
Scalability: Scalability is an important aspect of 3D grass models. They should be optimized for different viewing distances and performance requirements. For distant backgrounds, simplified versions of the grass may be used to maintain rendering efficiency.
Real-time Rendering Optimization: In applications like video games, where real-time rendering is crucial, techniques like impostors (2D representations of 3D objects) or LOD (level of detail) systems may be employed to ensure smooth performance while maintaining realism.
Seasonal Variation: For added realism, some models may include different grass variations for different seasons, with changes in color and density to represent spring, summer, autumn, or winter conditions.
Environmental Effects: Realistic 3D grass models can also interact with environmental effects like rain, snow, or fog. They may accumulate moisture or react to changes in temperature and lighting.
In summary, a realistic 3D grass model is a complex digital asset designed to replicate the appearance and behavior of natural grass in a virtual environment. It combines intricate geometry, detailed textures, animation, and material properties to create an immersive and lifelike representation of grassy landscapes in various 3D applications.

description_text:
Wooden carvingThis is wooden carving from Vietnam. Wood carving is a form of woodworking by means of a cutting tool (knife) in one hand or a chisel by two hands or with one hand on a chisel and one hand on a mallet, resulting in a wooden figure or figurine, or in the sculptural ornamentation of a wooden object. The phrase may also refer to the finished product, from individual sculptures to hand-worked mouldings composing part of a tracery.
The making of sculpture in wood has been extremely widely practised, but does not survive undamaged as well as the other main materials like stone and bronze, as it is vulnerable to decay, insect damage, and fire. Therefore, it forms an important hidden element in the art history of many cultures.[1] Outdoor wood sculptures do not last long in most parts of the world, so it is still unknown how the totem pole tradition developed. Many of the most important sculptures of China and Japan, in particular, are in wood, and so are the great majority of African sculpture and that of Oceania and other regions. Wood is light and can take very fine detail so it is highly suitable for masks and other sculpture intended to be worn or carried. It is also much easier to work on than stone and can be carved more thinly and precisely due to its fibrous strength.[2]
Some of the finest extant examples of early European wood carving are from the Middle Ages in Germany, Russia, Italy and France, where the typical themes of that era were Christian iconography. In England, many complete examples remain from the 16th and 17th century, where oak was the preferred medium.
The oldest wood carved sculpture, the Shigir Idol carved from larch, is around 12,000 years old.

DescriptionDescription Description Highly Detailed 3D scene of Leech Green Blood Cells flowing inside a Leech Blood Vessel Segment.
Created in 3ds Max 2022 and rendered with V-Ray.
This scene is a highly detailed setup of green blood cells flowing inside a blood vessel segment. An emitter at the beginning of the segment releases particles that flow along the curve of the vessel wall, which have been instanced with the blood cell polygonal geometry. The speed and amount of blood cells can be modified by adjusting the particle lifespan and rate attributes.
Camera and light sources that are included, additional stationary cameras and lights can be added anywhere inside the blood vessel walls.
These images have been rendered directly from the scene file, no post work is needed.
Close attention to detail makes this scene ideal for use in medical animations, broadcast, print work, advertising, design visualization, personal projects, etc.

description_text:
Beyond the spiral arms of the known galaxies, in the vaulted chambers of the Luminous Accord, the Mantis Envoy sits in silence—its vast, compound eyes shimmering with intelligence and memory older than stars. It has traveled across timefolded routes to observe, to speak in gestures, to offer peace and ancient wisdom. It carries no weapon, only ceremonial crests and inlaid ornaments—symbols of status and encoded diplomacy.
This highly detailed model represents an advanced extraterrestrial ambassador, mantis-like in physiology, bearing signs of civilization through embedded organic ornaments and crown-like antennae. A perfect choice for sci-fi collectors, tabletop settings, or storytelling figurines involving interspecies alliances, cosmic diplomacy, or alien mysteries.
Created with AI-assisted tools and extensively refined by hand in Blender and other 3D editing software to ensure precision, personality, and print-readiness.
Please note that the model is primarily designed for textured versions (OBJ + MTL in ZIP archive), allowing for a rich and visually detailed result when used with color-supported 3D printing or digital rendering. The non-textured version (STL, 3MF) may lack some surface details visible in the textured formats.
  - Technical Features and Printing Recommendations:
Recommended Print Size: 100–150 mm in height for tabletop scale
Support Needed: Yes, especially under the arms and antennae
Recommended Materials: PLA, Resin, or PETG for best detail
Minimum Print Time: ~120 minutes depending on scale
Material Use Estimate: ~25–35 grams at 100 mm height
Recommended Layer Height: 0.1–0.2 mm
Multi-material Print: Optional (useful for ornaments)
Color Printing: Best suited for full-color or painted post-processing
Scaling Note: This model is designed in millimeters (mm). If it appears too small when imported into your slicer, ensure your software is set to mm units. If needed, scale the model up 100x if the slicer defaults to meters instead.

This 3D model represents a highly realistic tarantula, designed for collectors, educational projects, and tabletop gaming. The figure captures the distinct features of a tarantula, including the robust body, articulated legs, and fine textural details across the carapace and limbs. The natural resting pose makes it ideal for dioramas, display, or as a reference piece for painting.
The model comes in both textured (OBJ + MTL) and non-textured (STL, 3MF) formats, providing options for those using color 3D printers as well as standard monochrome prints. All body parts, edges, and tips are clearly visible and separated for ease of painting or digital rendering.

Estimated Print Time: 2.5–5 hours, depending on size
Material Usage: 30–50g at standard scale
Scaling Note: This model is designed in millimeters (mm). If it appears too small when imported into your slicer, ensure your software is set to mm units. If needed, scale the model up 100x if the slicer defaults to meters instead.
Please note that the model is primarily designed for textured versions (OBJ + MTL in ZIP archive), allowing for a rich and visually detailed result when used with color-supported 3D printing or digital rendering. description_text:
In a small orchard, gardeners used to watch for the first ladybug of spring. When it landed on a leaf, they took it as a quiet sign that the season was turning in the right direction. Some even kept a tiny carving of the beetle near seed jars, hoping it would bring steady growth and fewer pests. This model is made in that spirit, as a simple nature charm you can print and keep on a shelf, desk, or diorama.
This 3D model depicts a realistic ladybug with a smooth domed shell, clear wing-case seam, and distinct black spots. The head and thorax have subtle surface texture, and the legs are sculpted with visible joints and a grounded stance. The body shape reads well from top view and front view, which makes it suitable for display, educational collections, tabletop scenery, or nature-themed décor.
This model is based on an original concept and design. The initial 3D form was generated with the assistance of AI tools, after which it was extensively refined and manually detailed in Blender and other 3D editing software. This workflow ensures the figure maintains its unique character and meets the standards of precision, structure, and print-readiness required for high-quality 3D printing.
Please note that the model is primarily designed for textured versions (OBJ + MTL in ZIP archive), allowing for a rich and visually detailed result when used with color-supported 3D printing or digital rendering. The non-textured version (STL, 3MF) may lack some surface details visible in the textured formats.
Technical features and printing recommendations
Recommended print settings (resin)
Layer height: 0.03–0.05 mm
Supports: light supports under legs and under the body edge
Orientation: slight angle to reduce peel forces on the shell
Material: standard resin or tough resin for stronger legs
Recommended print settings (FDM)
Layer height: 0.12–0.16 mm, 0.4 mm nozzle
Supports: supports under legs if printed as one piece
Material: PLA or PETG
Adhesion: brim suggested for small contact areas
Supports and assembly
Supports are recommended due to the thin legs and undercuts.
Print as a single piece for easiest display use.
If you scale down heavily, consider thicker support settings to protect the legs.
Clean-up focus areas: leg tips and underside of the shell rim.
Recommended size, time, material
Recommended size: 50–70 mm body length for a clear, sturdy print
Minimum print time to plan for: 180 minutes
Resin material estimate at ~60 mm: 20–35 g (varies with hollowing and supports)
Filament material estimate at ~60 mm: 12–25 g (varies with infill and supports)
Scaling Note: This model is designed in millimeters (mm). If it appears too small when imported into your slicer, ensure your software is set to mm units. If needed, scale the model up 100x if the slicer defaults to meters instead.

description_text:
In the drowned trenches beneath Aevaris, sailors speak of a creature that never travels alone, even when it is one body. They call it the Triarch Reef Stalker because each head seems to think separately, turning in different directions as if three minds are sharing a single hunt. When it rises from black water or broken coral, the first sign is the clicking of too many legs on stone. The second is silence, because everything nearby has already gone still.
Core Faction: The TidewalkersLore snippet: The Triarch Reef Stalker is said to patrol forgotten ruins below the tide line, where old prophecies were carved into shell and basalt long before the surface kingdoms learned to name the sea.
This model depicts a three-headed alien crustacean with a long segmented body, armored shell plates, and multiple hooked legs arranged in a dense, predatory stance. The front head is larger and more dominant, with bulbous eyes, mandible-like mouthparts, and hanging tendrils that give the creature a hostile, probing look. The rear heads reinforce the idea of a fused colony organism, each with its own facial structure and limb arrangement, making the silhouette unusual from every angle.
The body surface combines hard shell geometry with organic tissue transitions. Angular dorsal plates run along the spine, while softer membranes and ridged joints appear between leg segments and around the neck structures. The many limbs create a strong tabletop presence and help the creature feel unstable in a good way, like something built for reef ambushes, trench crawling, or alien brood behavior. It works well as a boss monster, a deep-sea horror, a sci-fi arthropod, or a display creature for collectors who like unsettling anatomy.
This model is based on an original concept and design. The initial 3D form was generated with the assistance of AI tools, after which it was extensively refined and manually detailed in Blender and other 3D editing software. This workflow ensures the figure maintains its unique character and meets the standards of precision, structure, and print-readiness required for high-quality 3D printing.
Please note that the model is primarily designed for textured versions (OBJ + MTL in ZIP archive), allowing for a rich and visually detailed result when used with color-supported 3D printing or digital rendering. The non-textured version (STL, 3MF) may lack some surface details visible in the textured formats.
Technical features and printing recommendations
Recommended print technology
Resin printers are best for preserving mandibles, tendrils, shell seams, and thin leg details.
FDM printers can handle it at larger scale, with careful support settings and slower outer walls.
Suggested resin settings
Layer height: 0.03–0.05 mm
Orientation: tilt 20–30° to reduce suction and protect the front head and underside
Supports: medium supports under legs, mouth tendrils, underside plates, and rear limb clusters
Hollowing: 2–3 mm wall thickness if scaled large, with drain holes hidden under the belly
Suggested FDM settings
Layer height: 0.12–0.16 mm with a 0.4 mm nozzle
Walls: 3 perimeters, infill 12–18%
Supports: required for legs, tendrils, and deep gaps between body segments
Material: PLA for easier printing, PETG for stronger limbs
Recommended size and print estimates
Recommended length: 120–180 mm for tabletop use, or 220–280 mm for display
Supports: required
Minimum print time: 480 minutes
Material estimate at about 160 mm length: Resin 120–190 g or Filament 140–220 g, depending on hollowing and infill
Scaling Note: This model is designed in millimeters (mm). If it appears too small when imported into your slicer, ensure your software is set to mm units. If needed, scale the model up 100x if the slicer defaults to meters instead.

description_text:
A playful 3D chromosome mascot named Helix performs a high-energy cartoon animation on a clean background.
The character suddenly spins down from above the frame with a fast corkscrew rotation and lands in the center with a soft, squash-and-stretch impact. After landing, Helix bounces slightly, stretches, squashes, wiggles happily, and makes energetic, playful poses with lots of personality.
During the animation, bold call-to-action messages appear one after another:Come PlayTest Your AppSec SkillsBeat the Challenge
Helix interacts with each message by pointing at it, jumping around it, peeking from behind it, or popping between the text transitions with fun cartoon expressions.
After a brief playful celebration, Helix coils into a spinning corkscrew, accelerates upward with a fast spiral motion, and flies out through the top of the frame, leaving a dynamic motion trail. The animation ends with the screen clean and ready for a seamless loop.
Style: Pixar-quality 3D animation, exaggerated squash and stretch, smooth anticipation and follow-through, expressive body language, energetic timing, polished cinematic lighting, clean composition, high-quality motion, 24 fps.
